transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corvik Holman.
Big tech company, Nvidia, has just announced that its CEO,
Jensen Huang, is stepping down.
This comes after Huang admitted to an affair.
News reports say that affair was with an alleged Chinese spy,
and PR has not confirmed that report.
NPR's John Ruich has more.
The decision follows a flurry of reports from The New York Times and others
alleging that Huang had had an extramarital affair with an executive at Nvidia,
and a separate one with a client who U.S. intelligence officials believed
was recruited by China's government to spy on him.
NPR has not independently confirmed those reports.
The departure ends a long career for Huang, who co-founded Nvidia 33 years ago
and oversaw its rise to become one of the world's biggest and most important companies.
News of Huang's affairs has rattled markets,
and Nvidia's share price has taken a beating in recent days.
John Ruich, NPR News.
Democrat Scott Colombe will be the next U.S. senator from Mississippi.
That is according to a race call from the Associated Press.
NPR's Stephen Fowler takes a look at Colombe's victory.
Black turnout surged in the South this year, but it really surged in Mississippi,
the state with the highest share of black voters in the country.
Several majority-black counties in Mississippi saw higher Democratic turnout this year
than the presidential race in 2024.
And overall, Colombe earned about 6,600 more raw votes this year
than former Vice President Kamala Harris.
That's more than his margin over Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith.
On the other side of the equation, Republican turnout plummeted with Hyde-Smith
receiving closer to 300,000 votes fewer than President Trump,
thanks to a combination of people switching their support to Colombe
and Republicans just staying home.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News.
Russia fired ballistic missiles at Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, overnight hours
after peace talks between Ukrainian and Russian negotiators concluded in Abu Dhabi.
U.S. negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Whitcoff traveled to Moscow
for talks with Russian President Putin that had to hire the next
to talk with Ukraine's president.
And Piers Eleanor Beardsley reports.
Ballistic missile explosions rocked Kyiv around 1 a.m.
and continued over the next hour as witnessed by NPR reporters in the city.
Ukraine no longer has enough interceptors to shoot them all down.
Russia has stepped up attacks on Ukraine's energy and transportation infrastructure,
especially in Kyiv, as it seeks to break the will of Ukrainians
during this fifth winter of war.
Speaking from Dublin, Ukrainian President Voludimir Zelensky
said the U.S. had been putting pressure on Ukraine to give up territory,
which he called "unacceptable."
Analysts say the Trump administration is especially keen
to conclude a peace deal after its drubbing in midterm elections.
Ukraine has said it is willing to accept freezing the front lines for a cease-fire,
but will not hand over the approximately quarter of the Donbass region
Russia has been unable to conquer.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv.
This is NPR.
New York City Mayor Zoran Mamdani says at least eight people have been killed
by the collapse of a building yesterday in Brooklyn.
He says another 17 people have been injured, including three firefighters.
Officials don't know how many more people may be trapped in the building's rubble,
and they don't know what triggered the collapse.
The American Cancer Society is changing its prostate screening guidelines.
NPR's Yuki Noguchi reports it's now recommending regular PSA blood test screenings for men.
The Cancer Society previously recommended patients talk to their doctors
and share decision-making about whether to screen for prostate cancer,
which will be diagnosed in roughly 333,000 Americans this year.
Now, based on new data, it recommends PSA tests every other year for men between 50 and 69,
and annual screenings starting at age 45 for those at high risk,
like black men and people with strong family history.
One concern was that prostate cancer, which can be harmless in many men,
was being overtreated, causing more harm than good.
To prevent that, the Cancer Society is also recommending MRI
and additional blood tests before getting a biopsy.
Yuki Noguchi, NPR News.
The U.N. Climate Summit is now underway in Turkey.
The U.N. Secretary General has exhorted delegates to step up efforts to combat climate change.
Scientists say that will increase the risk of catastrophic rises in sea levels worldwide
and collapse ecosystems.
I'm Cora Vekulman, NPR News.
This message comes from Angie.
Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years.
For everything from minor repairs to major remodels,
find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.

topics.text: Nvidia announces CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down amid reported affairs and spy allegations
Democrat Scott Colombe wins Mississippi Senate race, AP calls it, with surging Black turnout
Russia fires ballistic missiles at Kyiv after Abu Dhabi peace talks; Zelensky rejects territorial concessions
At least eight killed after Brooklyn building collapse; NYC Mayor Mamdani says 17 injured
American Cancer Society recommends regular PSA screening for men, changing prostate cancer guidelines
U.N. Climate Summit opens in Turkey; Secretary General urges faster action on climate change
